steps.title: Grind mesocarp with acetone mix
steps.instruction: Grind 10 g sliced mesocarp and mix with 25 mL cold acetone containing 10 % trichloroacetic acid and 1 mM dithiothreitol on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge slurry
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the slurry at 13 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C using a RA‑300 rotor (Kubota 7820).

steps.title: Wash pellet with methanol‑ammonium acetate
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL cold 80 % methanol containing 0.1 M ammonium acetate to the precipitate, mix well and centrifuge as before on ice; repeat the washing once.

steps.title: Wash pellet with cold acetone
steps.instruction: Wash the precipitated mesocarp pellet with 25 mL cold 80 % acetone, mix well and centrifuge again at 13 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the pellet in 15 mL extraction buffer containing 0.7 M sucrose, 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.3), 5 M NaCl, 50 mM DTT, 1 mM EDTA and one tablet of Roche protease inhibitors.

steps.title: Sonicate suspension
steps.instruction: Sonicate the suspension in an ultrasonic bath for 30 min (Townson & Mercer Ltd., England, UK).

steps.title: Phenol extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of fresh 50 mM Tris‑saturated phenol (pH 8.0, 15 mL) to the mixture, mix well and centrifuge at 15 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C (RA‑300 rotor, Kubota 7820) to separate phases.

steps.title: Precipitate phenol‑phase proteins
steps.instruction: To the upper phenol phase add five volumes of cold ammonium acetate‑saturated methanol (25 mL) per volume of phenol, mix well, incubate at –20 °C overnight and centrifuge at 15 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C (RA‑300 rotor, Kubota 7820).

steps.title: Rinse and wash protein pellet
steps.instruction: Rinse the protein pellet with 5 mL cold ammonium acetate‑saturated methanol, then wash three times with 5 mL cold 80 % acetone and air‑dry for 5 min.

steps.title: Add evaluated solubilization buffers
steps.instruction:
Add 600 µL of each evaluated buffer to separate aliquots of the protein pellet:
• Buffer A: 7 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 4 % CHAPS, 0.4 % DTT, 10 mM Tris
• Buffer B: 7 M urea, 4 % CHAPS, 0.4 % DTT, 10 mM Tris
• Buffer C: 7 M urea, 4 % sodium deoxycholate, 0.4 % DTT, 10 mM Tris
• Buffer D: 4 % sodium deoxycholate, 0.4 % DTT, 10 mM Tris.

steps.title: Quantify protein content
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration with the commercial 2D Quant Kit (GE Healthcare Life Sciences) using the supplied BSA standard; perform each quantitation in duplicate.

steps.title: Re‑precipitate for digestion (50 µg)
steps.instruction: Re‑precipitate the solubilized proteins with cold ammonium acetate‑saturated methanol to obtain 50 µg protein for in‑solution digestion.

steps.title: Resuspend and reduce/alkylate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the precipitated proteins in 0.1 M ammonium bicarbonate and 1 M urea; reduce with 50 mM tris(2‑carboxyethyl)phosphine and alkylate with 150 mM iodoacetamide.

steps.title: Add deoxycholate and digest
steps.instruction: Add sodium deoxycholate to a final concentration of 1 % (w/v) and digest with 4 µg modified sequencing‑grade trypsin (Promega) in 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ for 16 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Remove deoxycholate post‑digestion
steps.instruction: Acidify the digest with 0.5 % formic acid and centrifuge at 14 000 g (RA‑300, Kubota 7820) for 15 min at ambient temperature to precipitate and remove sodium deoxycholate.

steps.title: Dry peptide solution
steps.instruction: Dry the supernatant peptide solution in a centrifugal evaporator (CentriVap Concentrator, Labconco).

steps.title: Resuspend peptides
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried peptide pellet in 200 µL of 0.1 % formic acid.

steps.title: Solid‑phase extraction on C18
steps.instruction: Add Empore C18 SPE disks conditioned with acetonitrile, methanol and 0.1 % formic acid to the peptide solution; incubate at ambient temperature with slight agitation for 4 h.

steps.title: Elute bound peptides
steps.instruction: Sequentially elute the bound peptides from the C18 membrane with 50 % acetonitrile in 0.1 % formic acid for 2.5 h.

steps.title: Re‑precipitate for 1‑D gel (100 µg)
steps.instruction: Re‑precipitate the solubilized proteins with cold ammonium acetate‑saturated methanol to obtain 100 µg protein for electrophoresis.

steps.title: Prepare sample for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Dissolve the precipitated proteins in Laemmli buffer (62.5 mM Tris‑HCl pH 6.8, 2 % SDS, 25 % glycerol, 0.01 % bromophenol blue, 0.005 % β‑mercaptoethanol) and boil at 95 °C for 4 min.

steps.title: Load and run gel
steps.instruction: Load 100 µg protein per lane onto an in‑house cast 12 % polyacrylamide gel (1.0 mm thickness) and perform electrophoresis.

steps.title: Fix, stain and destain gel
steps.instruction: Fix the gel for 30 min in 50 % ethanol / 10 % acetic acid, stain with in‑house colloidal Coomassie G‑250, then destain with Milli‑Q water until the background is clear.

steps.title: Scan gel image
steps.instruction: Scan the stained gel with a Bio‑5000 Plus scanner (Microtek) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Reconstitute tryptic digests
steps.instruction: Reconstitute dried tryptic digests in 20 µL of 0.1 % formic acid containing 5 % acetonitrile.

steps.title: Load onto LC column
steps.instruction: Inject 2 µL of the reconstituted digest onto an Acclaim PepMap 100 C18 column (3 µm, 0.075 × 150 mm).

steps.title: Equilibrate column and run gradient
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the column with 95 % mobile phase A (0.1 % formic acid) and 5 % mobile phase B (80 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid); elute peptides with a linear gradient from 5 % to 35 % B over 70 min at 300 nL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Set MS acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Generate peptide ions with a spray voltage of 1800 V; scan m/z 310–1800 at 70 000 resolving power, maximum injection time 100 ms, selecting charge states 2–8 for fragmentation.

steps.title: Set MS fragmentation parameters
steps.instruction: Fragment ions with a scan rate resolution of 14 500, isolation window 0.7 m/s, maximum injection time 60 ms, scan m/z 110–1800; use normalized collision energy of 28 % for both CID and HCD.

steps.title: Process raw data
steps.instruction: Acquire data in positive mode with Xcalibur v4.1.31.9; process RAW files in Proteome Discoverer 2.1.

steps.title: Database search parameters (first set)
steps.instruction: Search MS2 spectra with SEQUEST™ HT against the Magnoliophyta taxonomy (35 391 reviewed proteins, 13 July 2017) in SWISSPROT; set peptide mass tolerance 10 ppm, product ion tolerance 0.6 Da; allow up to two missed cleavages; fixed modification carbamidomethylation on cysteine; variable modifications oxidation (Met) and deamidation (Asn, Gln).

steps.title: Database search parameters (second set)
steps.instruction: Search MS2 spectra with SEQUEST HT against Elaeis guineensis and Phoenix dactylifera NCBI protein databases; set peptide mass tolerance 20 ppm, product ion tolerance 0.5 Da; allow up to two missed cleavages; fixed modifications carbamidomethylation on cysteine and lysine; variable modifications oxidation (Met) and deamidation (Asn, Gln).

steps.title: Validate peptide‑spectral matches
steps.instruction: Accept proteins with at least one Rank 1 peptide; perform decoy‑database searches to estimate false discovery rate; validate PSMs with Percolator v2.04 at 1 % FDR.

steps.title: Generate Venn diagram and GO annotation
steps.instruction: Create a Venn diagram of identified proteins using Venny 2.1 (or http://bioinformatics.psb.ugent.be/webtools/Venn); annotate biological process, cellular component and molecular function with the STRAP program (or Uniprot Retrieve/ID mapping tool).

steps.title: Perform supervised PLS‑DA
steps.instruction: Use MetaboAnalyst (version 3.0 or 4.9) to conduct supervised partial least‑squares discriminant analysis correlating protein peak intensities with solubilization buffers; sum peaks per sample (32 614 groups), group variables by retention time (mass tolerance 0.025 m/z, RT tolerance 30 s), filter with interquartile range, normalize by sum of intensities and apply Pareto scaling.

steps.title: Validate PLS‑DA model
steps.instruction: Validate the PLS‑DA model by permutation test (100 permutations); for each model compute between/within sum‑of‑squares ratio, plot the distribution as a histogram to assess significance.
